articles.title: Gratitude makes people more helpful, but it doesn’t overcome the bystander effect
articles.summary: A new study published in Cognition and Emotion indicates that while gratitude boosts your overall willingness to help someone in need, it doesn't overcome the bystander effect. Even grateful people hesitate when a crowd is present.

articles.title: Psychological distress isolates men more than women, according to a 14-year study
articles.summary: Social support boosts mental health for both sexes, but a new study shows men face a unique trap. When experiencing psychological distress, men are far more likely than women to withdraw and lose their social safety nets.

articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary: A prescription form of THC helped many people with PTSD escape recurring trauma-related nightmares, with more than one-third reporting that the nightmares disappeared completely after ten weeks. The results could point toward a long-awaited treatment for one of PTSD’s most distressing and stubborn symptoms.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary: A long-term brain study found that common risks such as smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids were strongly linked to damage associated with vascular dementia. The findings suggest that healthier lifestyle choices could help delay dementia by reducing several harmful brain changes at once.

articles.title: Brief DMT trips linked to lasting improvements in quality of life for depressed patients
articles.summary: A new study indicates that brief experiences with inhaled DMT can reduce anxiety and improve life satisfaction. For patients with treatment-resistant depression, the substance combined with therapy might promote long-lasting enhancements in overall quality of life.

articles.title: Animal studies suggest that reproductive behavior fully recovers after puberty-blocking treatment ends
articles.summary: Temporarily pausing puberty with leuprolide in adolescent rats delays reproductive development. However, research in Biology of Sex Differences and Hormones and Behavior provides evidence that subjects achieve full physical and behavioral maturation after treatment ends.

articles.title: Your brain may be wired to regain lost weight
articles.summary: Weight loss is not simply a test of willpower. The human brain evolved to protect body fat during times of scarcity, and it can treat a previously higher weight as the new normal, triggering stronger hunger, cravings, and lower energy use after weight loss. This biological “memory” helps explain why many people regain weight after dieting and why medications such as Wegovy and Mounjaro can help by reducing appetite signals, although their effects may fade when treatment ends.

articles.title: A climate-friendly diet might protect your brain by slowing cellular aging
articles.summary: Eating a climate-friendly diet packed with plants might do more than protect the environment. A large study found that strict adherence to sustainable eating habits is associated with a lower risk of stroke, depression, and anxiety.

articles.title: Many video game trolls are actually just vigilantes acting on a misunderstanding, study suggests
articles.summary: New research suggests much of the toxic behavior in online video games stems from a simple misunderstanding. When players misinterpret ambiguous actions as trolling, they often retaliate, accidentally sparking a contagious cycle of digital harassment.

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary: A simple change in posture may subtly affect how people feel and make decisions. Participants who sat upright reported greater feelings of pride and took more successful risks in a virtual balloon game than those who hunched over. Most did not realize researchers had influenced their posture, helping rule out the possibility that they were merely responding to expectations. The results suggest workplace ergonomics could influence more than physical comfort.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary: A group of brain cells called orexin neurons appears to help us keep working when reaching a reward becomes increasingly difficult. Blocking their activity weakened motivation in rats, pointing to a possible new target for understanding why people sometimes struggle to sustain goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: How a year abroad shapes student personality
articles.summary: Spending a year studying abroad makes college students more agreeable, curious, and less anxious. A recent study tracked students' daily habits and discovered that these momentary behaviors gradually accumulate to shape long-term personality development.
